question: Which state won the first prize among states in Group 1 for energy efficiency at the National Energy Conservation Awards (NECA) 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Karnataka.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__** 

__
 
• **Karnataka won the first prize among states in Group 1 for energy efficiency at the National Energy Conservation Awards (NECA) 2025, presented by President Droupadi Murmu on National Energy Conservation Day.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__
 
• **The 35th edition of NECA was organized by the Bureau of Energy Efficiency under the Ministry of Power.**
 
• **The awards recognized contributions from industries, buildings, and other sectors for sustainable energy practices.**
 
• **President Murmu highlighted India's progress in energy conservation, including saving 53.60 million tonnes of oil equivalent in 2023-24.**
 
• **Karnataka topped the states list, followed by Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Assam, and Chandigarh in other groups.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

__
 
• **National Energy Conservation Awards (NECA)**__

 __
 
• Annual awards recognizing excellence in energy efficiency across states, industries, and buildings.
 
• Organized by the Bureau of Energy Efficiency under the Ministry of Power, India.
 
 
 
• **LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment)**__
 __
 
• Government initiative promoting sustainable lifestyles and energy-conscious behavior.
 
• Encourages citizens to adopt energy-saving practices in daily life.
 
 
 
• **Key Government Initiatives**__
 __
 
• Pradhan Mantri Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana – promotes rooftop solar installations.
 
• National Green Hydrogen Mission – aims to reduce fossil fuel dependence.
 
 
 
• **Energy Savings Achievement**__
 
 
• India saved 53.60 million tonnes of oil equivalent in 2023-24 through energy efficiency measures.
